subject: Request: Auto-revert + Version-pin for EU latency spike during A/B rollout
messages:
From: Emma Shaw <emma@skybridge.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@skybridge.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden p95 spike in EU during A/B — request for auto-revert + pin

Hi Markus,

We started seeing regressions in p95 latency for our EU traffic after the A/B rollout you helped schedule this morning. The canary was at 8% when we first noticed a jump from ~180ms to ~720-900ms p95. The spike coincides with a model variant (v2-quant) that was introduced as part of the experiment.

I attached a short metrics snapshot from our monitoring window — you can see the step-change around 14:05 UTC. This is affecting production user flows (checkout) and our internal SLAs.

Can you (a) enable an immediate auto-revert for the canary if p95 > 600ms for 3 consecutive minutes, and (b) pin the stable model version for EU traffic until we finish a deeper postmortem?

We appreciate a quick confirmation and an ETA for when those mitigations will be live.

Thanks,
Emma Shaw
Head of Platform Reliability
Skybridge AI
Attachments: metrics-snapshot-2026-06-27.png (image/png)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Shaw <emma@skybridge.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike in EU during A/B — request for auto-revert + pin

Emma — thanks for the heads up and the graph. I’ve looped Vanessa (runtime ops) and Lauren (product) to move this to action.

Quick responses to your asks:
- Auto-revert: we can implement a safety rule that triggers an immediate rollback of the canary traffic to the pinned stable model when p95 > 600ms for 3 minutes.
- Pin stable: we can pin the last known-good model (stable:v1.14) for all EU routes until the postmortem.

Before we flip anything: please confirm you approve the rollback policy below (we’ll execute it within the next 25 minutes after confirmation):
- Trigger: p95 >= 600ms for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows
- Scope: eu-west-1 region only, traffic fraction revert to 0% for canary variant
- Rollback target: stable:v1.14 (pinned)
- Safety check: verify KV cache compatibility — we’ll run a quick compatibility probe before final cutover (5 min).

If you approve, Vanessa will post the change and run the rollback. Lauren — can you confirm the pinning call and we’ll record the change in the rollout audit?

Markus
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
(on-call: +1-555-0103)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Emma Shaw <emma@skybridge.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 02:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike in EU during A/B — request for auto-revert + pin

On Sun, 27 Jun 2026 at 17:03 -0400, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Emma — thanks for the heads up and the graph. I’ve looped Vanessa (runtime ops) and Lauren (product) to move this to action.
>
> Quick responses to your asks:...

Thanks — I’m taking this as action owner for the mitigation. Action plan and exact run commands below. I’ll execute as soon as Emma confirms acceptance of the rollback policy.

Summary of planned mitigation (will be applied to EU only):
1) Canary auto-revert policy:
   - Metric: request_p95_latency_ms (aggregated at 1m)
   - Condition: p95 >= 600 for 3 consecutive 1m intervals
   - Response: immediate traffic revert to pinned stable variant; mark canary as 'inactive' in the rollout
2) Version pin:
   - Pin stable:v1.14 on EU routes via pinned-model override in the routing table
   - Lock will be annotated for 72 hours and requires manual unpin + rollout plan to resume experiments
3) Safety probes before final cutover (automated, ~5 min):
   - KV cache consistency check (probe against a small sample set)
   - Health-check traffic (synthetic) to validate p50/p95 after revert
4) Post-action:
   - Postmortem ticket (RWD-INC-2026-06-27-042) opened and assigned to runtime + model infra for triage
   - Canary config diff attached and will be committed to the customer audit log

Operational notes (risks & mitigations):
- If the revert does not reduce p95, we will enable fallback to a lighter quantized variant (stable:q1) and throttle background batching.
- We will not change global routing — scope is strictly eu-west-1 to avoid cascading effects.

Attachments: canary-config.diff (text)
Runbook: DOC-OPS-RUNBOOK-42 (internal)
Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/skybridge/samples/rollouts/98765

I’ll wait for Emma’s approval to proceed now. If I don’t hear back in 15 minutes, I’ll start the safety probes and be ready to flip if triggered by our alerts.

— Vanessa
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
Pager: +1-555-0321

From: Emma Shaw <emma@skybridge.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike in EU during A/B — request for auto-revert + pin

Marked approved — please proceed with the auto-revert + pin as described.

A couple quick asks before you flip:
- Please confirm the exact timestamp when the revert happens and call out any expected 2xx->5xx risk window during the cache probe.
- We’d like to request a 5% service credit if the incident meets our SLA criteria (we track p95 > 500ms for 15 minutes as an incident threshold). If your postmortem finds the deployment variant caused the regression, we’ll expect credits tied to that window.

Thanks all — we rely on this rollout framework being safe and reversible. Please copy our platform ops (ops@skybridge.ai) in the final status update.

Emma
Head of Platform Reliability, Skybridge AI
Attachments: none
